messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: precompiling Stan as object code
parts:
[back on stan-dev]

On 12/1/13, 5:35 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:

>> The only thing I was thinking about doing was using
>> template instantiations as we do for the grammars
>> so these become one-time speed costs at the expense of
>> using much more memory. This is just the template lib
>> version of breaking a lib into .cpp and .hpp file.
>
> Is it not possible to do the same thing with the rest of Stan the library? Like instantiate one dynamically resizeable
> Cholesky object with our scalar types?

It's pretty straightforward. Especially for Cholesky,
which only has two instantiations until we add RHMC,
namely Matrix<double> and Matrix<var>.

The problem is that we have a lot of functions and many of
them are far more polymorphic than the Cholesky decomposition.

The worst case is for now is the Student-t density function,
which has four arguments, each of which can be instantiated by

double, var,
vector<double>, vector<var>,
row-vector<double>, row-vector<var>,
vector<var>, vector<double>, for a total of 8^4 (4096) instantiations.

I don't think that will be feasible in terms of compilation time
or object code size.

With the header-based approach we take now, only the instances that
are used in a particular model get instantiated and compiled, though
it has to be done on a model-per-model basis.

- Bob

I see what you are saying about instantiating the density functions, but can we do something about instantiating the classes we use? I have been reading about the "extern template" syntax, which is now part of the c++11 standard but has been a gcc-ism since version 3.3, so it should work with the llvm-g++-4.2 on Macs and the mingw-4.6 on Windows. This basically does explicit instantiation once and then blocks implicit instantiation in the files that use those classes.

There is a recipe for it here

http://books.google.com/books?id=gCn0wqT4W14C&lpg=PT472&ots=H8T2VMlz2O&dq=c%2B%2B11%20%22extern%20template%22&pg=PT471#v=onepage&q&f=false

and a FAQ here

http://www.stroustrup.com/C++11FAQ.html#extern-templates

Ben

We're not really doing any dynamic linking (except of a complete

case the proposal talks about.

Where would we put the "extern template" declaration? And what compilation
would it suppress?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: precompiling Stan as object code
parts:
On Sunday, January 19, 2014 6:30:40 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
On Tue, Jan 14, 2014 at 8:46 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
Where would we put the "extern template" declaration?  And what compilation
would it suppress?

I'm curious about this also. What would "extern template" buy us in terms of saving compilation time?

My understanding is that we have things like

Eigen::Matrix<var,Eigen::Dynamic,Eigen::Dynamic>

all over the place and the compiler has to generate a lot of code every time one of those functions gets invoked. So, the extern template mechanism outlined in the Boost recipes book tries to make it such that you can tell the compiler to generate all the necessary code for that type once in a file that gets #included by files that need it.

Ben
